hero.description: Wat Visoun is a shorter temple visit with unusually useful historical weight: founded in the early sixteenth century, rebuilt after the 1887 destruction of Luang Prabang and paired with the rounded That Makmo stupa, it shows a different architectural chapter from Wat Xieng Thong.
steps: Look for the older Buddha images
hero.rhythmNote: Do not expect the same visual drama as Wat Xieng Thong. Come here for age, reconstruction history and the distinctive stupa.
hero.photoNote: Visoun village · south-east of the peninsula

route.secondary: a few minutes beyond the peninsula

chapters.label: THE CONTRAST
chapters.title: Come here after Wat Xieng Thong, not instead of it
chapters.body: Wat Visoun was founded in 1512 under King Visounnarath and belongs to an earlier architectural chapter of Luang Prabang. The original wooden structure was destroyed during the 1887 attack on the city and later rebuilt, so the temple is valuable partly because it carries both early history and the memory of reconstruction.

note.label: ATLAS NOTE
note.text: The rounded That Makmo stupa is the visual reason to linger; the temple’s history is the reason to come.

items.label: Time
items.detail: Enough for the sim, Buddha images and a circuit around That Makmo.

items.label: Access
items.value: Walk or bicycle from the centre
items.detail: It sits outside the peninsula but remains an easy in-town stop.

items.label: Best pairing
items.value: Wat Aham or a wider old-town circuit
items.detail: Use it as a compact historical contrast rather than building a separate outing around it.

items.label: Dress
items.detail: Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes where indicated and respect active religious space.

faq.question: Why visit Wat Visoun if I already saw Wat Xieng Thong?
faq.answer: Because it represents a different architectural and historical chapter. Wat Visoun is older in origin and is closely associated with the distinctive That Makmo stupa.

faq.question: What is That Makmo?
faq.answer: It is the rounded stupa in the temple grounds, often called the watermelon stupa because of its shape.

faq.question: How long do I need?
faq.answer: Around 45 minutes to one hour is enough for most visitors.

faq.question: Was the temple rebuilt?
faq.answer: Yes. The original temple was destroyed during the 1887 attack on Luang Prabang and reconstructed afterward.
